method: Each claim checked against the retrieved abstract text of its cited source, not the citation.

claims.claim: Defined by depressed mood, loss of interest, associated psychological and somatic symptoms lasting at least 2 weeks
claims.source_text: Major depression is defined by depressed mood, loss of interest in activities, and associated psychological and somatic symptoms lasting at least 2 weeks

claims.claim: Evaluation includes severity and risk of self-harm, suspected bipolar, psychotic symptoms, substance use, co-occurring anxiety
claims.source_text: Evaluation should include structured assessment of severity as well as risk of self-harm, suspected bipolar disorder, psychotic symptoms, substance use, and co-occurring anxiety disorder

claims.claim: First-line treatments include specific psychotherapies and antidepressant medications
claims.source_text: First-line treatments include specific psychotherapies and antidepressant medications

claims.claim: Six named psychotherapies had at least medium-sized effects over usual care, SMD 0.50 (0.20-0.81) to 0.73 (0.52-0.95)
claims.source_text: cognitive therapy, behavioral activation, problem-solving therapy, interpersonal therapy, brief psychodynamic therapy, and mindfulness-based psychotherapy all had at least medium-sized effects in symptom improvement over usual care without psychotherapy (standardized mean difference [SMD] ranging from 0.50 [95% CI, 0.20-0.81] to 0.73 [95% CI, 0.52-0.95])

claims.claim: 21 antidepressants had small- to medium-sized effects over placebo, SMD 0.23 (0.19-0.28) fluoxetine to 0.48 (0.41-0.55) amitriptyline
claims.source_text: 21 antidepressant medications all had small- to medium-sized effects in symptom improvement over placebo (SMD ranging from 0.23 [95% CI, 0.19-0.28] for fluoxetine to 0.48 [95% CI, 0.41-0.55] for amitriptyline)

claims.claim: Psychotherapy combined with medication may be preferred, especially for more severe or chronic depression
claims.source_text: Psychotherapy combined with antidepressant medication may be preferred, especially for more severe or chronic depression

claims.claim: S1 compared 21 antidepressants for acute treatment of adults with unipolar MDD, published and unpublished double-blind RCTs, placebo-controlled and head-to-head
claims.source_text: We included placebo-controlled and head-to-head trials of 21 antidepressants used for the acute treatment of adults (>=18 years old and of both sexes) with major depressive disorder ... published and unpublished, double-blind, randomised controlled trials

claims.claim: S1 excluded bipolar, psychotic and treatment-resistant depression, and serious concomitant medical illness
claims.source_text: We excluded quasi-randomised trials and trials that were incomplete or included 20% or more of participants with bipolar disorder, psychotic depression, or treatment-resistant depression; or patients with a serious concomitant medical illness

claims.claim: Antidepressants used more frequently than psychological interventions because of inadequate resources
claims.source_text: because of inadequate resources, antidepressants are used more frequently than psychological interventions

claims.claim: PBS: amitriptyline unrestricted; SSRIs/SNRIs restricted; vortioxetine and agomelatine not listed
claims.source_text: Schedule 4333 items query: Amitriptyline 17 rows ['U']; Sertraline 68 ['R']; Escitalopram 86 ['R']; Fluoxetine 16 ['R']; Mirtazapine 44 ['R']; Venlafaxine 35 ['R']; Desvenlafaxine 40 ['R']; Vortioxetine no rows; Agomelatine no rows

claims.claim: Psychotherapy and antidepressant effect sizes use different comparators and cannot be compared directly
claims.source_text: ...over usual care without psychotherapy (SMD 0.50-0.73)... vs ...over placebo (SMD 0.23-0.48)...
claims.note: Comparator difference is stated verbatim in the source; the inference that they are non-comparable is analytical, not a new empirical claim.
